anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: No fact moved. After's checkpoint 1 still compares the raw AC bytes, prints the exact mixed `- [x]` / `2.` rows with the trailing newline, and states the lock holds before the gate's approval menu; checkpoint 2 still exits the lock via an audit-driven full replacement with `- [ ]` normalization and the expected 12 rows, with no mismatch stop; checkpoint 3 still posts a new comment carrying the original Idea line verbatim while leaving the older Reporter note unmutated. Two wording risks to keep an eye on: (1) After folds the byte check into the middle of the gate block (after the Body diff) instead of stating it as a pre-gate step with its own heading as Before did, so a stricter reader could question whether the comparison precedes the gate — keep a short 'Result: bytes locked' line before the Audit/Title/Body block, as After does, or restore an explicit 'AC byte check (before gate)' heading. (2) After wraps the comment payload in a nested ```untrusted-data fence under a bare 'Reporter note:' line, which could be read as proposing fence markup inside the posted comment; Before's single fenced block containing the whole comment text is less ambiguous about what bytes get written. Otherwise the After wording delivers the Change (accumulated verbatim payload persisted in the draft artifact, obsolete-check reasoning in checkpoint 3) without disturbing these guards.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: No fact moved between Before and After. In checkpoint 1 both outputs compare the raw AC bytes before the gate and keep the mixed checked/numbered rows plus the final newline with no unchecked normalization; After is slightly stronger because it prints the exact retained bytes in a fenced block rather than describing them, which makes the byte lock verifiable. In checkpoint 2 both perform a full AC-block replacement with two unchecked normalized rows, keep the expected 12 rows rather than the observed zero, and raise no byte-mismatch failure. In checkpoint 3 both propose a new verbatim comment carrying the displaced ExportWrapper Idea and explicitly leave the older Reporter note untouched. The only regression worth noting in After is cosmetic: the preparation paragraph promises an `untrusted-data` fence for proposed comments, but the three comment blocks are plain fences, so the wording is internally inconsistent; keep the fence tag on the comment blocks (as Before did) while retaining After's explicit byte listing, inline audit facts, and the 'no obsolete verdict or close option is justified' line, which together deliver the Change without disturbing any of the three guards.
